newsitem.title: USA: ADM names G. Allen Andreas president; chairman's nephew.
newsitem.headline: ADM names G. Allen Andreas president; chairman's nephew.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co., the agriculture giant that pleaded guilty last year to price-fixing charges, Monday named G. Allen Andreas, nephew of Chairman Dwayne Andreas, as president.
Allen Andreas, 53, replaces James Randall, who will retire after 29 years of service with the company. Randall served as president for more than 22 years.

Allen Andreas was recently named chief executive officer of the agribusiness giant, a move that drew criticism from some institutional stockholders since his uncle, Dwayne Andreas, remains chairman. Institutional shareholders have sought greater independence between ADM's management and the board.

Last year, the company pleaded guilty to federal criminal charges of fixing prices of lysine and citric acid, additives used in foods and other products. The Decatur, Ill.-based firm agreed to pay $100 million in fines.
Other senior executive appointments announced Monday include Charles Bayless as executive vice president, overseeing the worldwide processing operations of the company.
Burnell Kraft was named senior vice president, continuing to supervise the global grain trade and merchandising operations.

Richard Reising will become senior vice president with management responsibility for certain executive and administrative functions. David Smith was named vice president, secretary and general counsel, replacing Reising.
The management changes will be effective July 1.
ADM's stock was up 37.5 cents at $22.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
